newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wall St tremors knock HK stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Wall St tremors knock HK stocks to lower close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply lower on Friday, shaken by Wall Street's deep dive and the spectre of an uptrend in U.S. and local lending rates, brokers said.
"This is a reaction to the meltdown on the Street," said one broker with a U.S. house. "We gapped down at the open and straight through the first line of support at 12,720."

The Hang Seng Index ended 180.56 points, or 1.4 percent, lower at 12,736.53 after opening at 12,723.83 and touching a low of 12,630.15. Turnover was a heavy HK$12.52 billion, about 20 percent higher than Thursday's HK$10.23 billion.
"It is early days yet but we may be seeing a change in sentiment in New York and Hong Kong and that is to sell into rallies rather than buy on dips," the U.S. broker said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 160 points to 6,878.89 on Thursday -- the fifth steepest fall in point terms in the history of the average.

The U.S. bond market, reacting to stronger than expected U.S. retail sales figures for February, closed 30/32 lower at 95-26/32 to yield 6.96 percent. It was the highest level in nearly six months, signalling near-term upside for interest rates, brokers said.
Not all brokers had turned bearish.
"The market has come off from 13,500 and that is a long way to discount an interest rate hike," said Francis Wong, executive director at DBS Securities.
Chartists, while surprised at how easily the cash and futures market crashed through 12,880, saw good support at around 12,600. Resistance now lies at 13,000 and 13,300.
The March Hang Seng Index futures contract closed 155 points lower at 12,690, a 46-point discount to the cash market.
The commercial and industrial sector was the worst performing, followed by properties.
Hutchison Whampoa led the field, falling HK$1.50 to HK$54.25. Swire Pacific lost HK$1.25 to HK$61.50.
Swire reported an 18.6 percent rise in 1996 net earnings to HK$7.65 billion, including exceptional gains of HK$1.58 billion.
New World Development recovered its intraday losses to close unchanged at HK$42.20, while all the other major property developers closed sharply down.
Cheung Kong, Henderson Land and Sun Hung Kai Properties all lost HK$1.50 to close at HK$69.00 and HK$63.00 and HK$83.50, respectively.
